h1: The 5 Best Personal Small Safes of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Personal Small Safes 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five personal small safes, from mountable keypad boxes to portable travel cases, sorted by lock type, size and price tier.
summary: The Bonsaii is the best personal small safe: a 0.23 cu ft bolt-down steel keypad box with USB-C emergency power for $25 to $50. The Voncabay adds a lockout after three wrong codes, and the Yuanshikj is the cheapest mountable box. The Master Lock and Amazon Basics are portable cases for travel.
intro: A small safe fails in two quiet ways. Either the whole box walks out the door because it was never bolted down, or its owner is locked out the day the battery dies. Neither failure shows up in the photos, and both are easy to avoid once you know to check mounting hardware and backup access on the spec sheet.

We ranked five personal safes on mounting, lock type, backup entry and price tier, using figures from the listings alone, not marketing claims. Three are keypad boxes meant to be fixed in place, and two are portable combination cases for travel. None lists fire protection, so read every pick as a theft deterrent for papers and small valuables, not a vault.

products.name: Bonsaii Small Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Valuables, 0.23 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: A mountable steel box with a USB-C emergency power option.
products.description:
The Bonsaii is a 0.23 cu ft mountable steel box with an electronic keypad, pre-drilled holes and a USB-C emergency power port. That port matters more than it looks. Keypad safes fail when the batteries go flat, and a port lets you push power in from a power bank and open the door. Price: the $25 to $50 bucket.

It ranks above the Voncabay because USB-C solves the worst keypad-safe problem outright. The Voncabay warns you the battery is low, which helps, but a warning is not a way in once the cells are dead. Against the Yuanshikj, the Bonsaii spends a bucket more for that rescue and a keypad listing with more features.

Buy it for a bedroom, closet or desk drawer where you can bolt it down. The caveat is capacity: 0.23 cu ft holds passports and papers, not a laptop. Skip it if you store bulky items.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants a bolt-down keypad safe with a lockout rescue.
products.skipIf: You need to store bulky items.

products.name: Voncabay Money Safe Box for Home with Digital Keypad, 0.23 Cu. Ft., Black
products.verdict: Smart guardrails: interior light, battery warning and a wrong-code lockout.
products.description:
The Voncabay Money Safe is a 0.23 cu ft mountable steel box with a digital keypad, plus guardrails the others lack. An automatic interior light helps in a dark closet, a low-battery warning arrives before the keypad fails, and three wrong entries trigger a five minute lockout. That lockout stops anyone from tapping through codes quickly. It sells in the $25 to $50 bucket.

Second place trails the Bonsaii because a warning about the battery is not a USB-C route back in, and the Voncabay lists none. The Bonsaii listing does not mention any lockout, so the Voncabay wins on brute-force resistance and the Bonsaii wins on recovery. Both share the same small interior.

Buy it for homes with curious children or frequent guests. The caveat is that it relies on the batteries you replace on time. Skip it if emergency power matters most.
products.idealFor: Homes with curious kids or frequent guests.
products.skipIf: You want an emergency power port.

products.name: Yuanshikj Small Steel Security Safe Box with Keypad, Key, 0.23 CuFt, Black
products.verdict: The cheapest mountable box here, with two steel locking bolts.
products.description:
The Yuanshikj is the cheapest way to get a bolt-down safe, at under $25. It is a 0.2 cu ft steel box whose door is held by two steel locking bolts and closed by a magnet, with pre-drilled holes and mounting hardware included. The twin bolts hold the door in two places, and the magnet closes it without a latch you must remember to push. The listing also includes a key.

It ranks third because it lacks the Bonsaii's USB-C backup and the Voncabay's lockout. Those cost a tier more, and this box skips them. Against the portable cases below, it still beats them on theft resistance, because a bolted steel box cannot be lifted and carried off the way a tethered or loose case can.

Buy it as a first safe or for a dorm drawer. The caveat is fewer conveniences, so keep the spare key somewhere separate. Skip it if you want battery warnings.
products.skipIf: You want battery warnings or backup power.

products.name: Master Lock Small Travel Safe with Cable, Gray Combination Lock Box, 5900D
products.verdict: A tethered combination box for hotels, cars and gym bags.
products.description:
The Master Lock 5900D is a small travel safe with a tether cable, a 4-digit combination that needs no key or battery, a charging cable access port and water resistance. The tether lets you loop the box around a fixed object in a hotel room or car. It sells in the under $25 bucket.

It ranks below the mountable boxes because a cable is easier to defeat than a bolt through a wall or shelf. It wins on portability, which the Bonsaii, Voncabay and Yuanshikj cannot offer, and on the charging port that lets a phone charge while locked up. Against the Amazon Basics case, the tether is the key difference, since that case lists none.

Buy it for hotels, gyms and road trips where you can anchor the cable. The caveat is plain: treat it as a deterrent, not a vault. Skip it for permanent home storage.
products.idealFor: Travelers who want a locking box for hotels and cars.
products.skipIf: You need a fixed home safe.

products.name: Amazon Basics Portable Security Case Lock Box Safe with Combination Lock
products.verdict: An anti-pry steel case with a foam-padded interior.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics Portable Security Case is a steel box with anti-pry construction, a foam-padded interior and a zinc alloy combination lock. Unlike the keypad boxes above, a combination dial needs no battery, and the padding protects cameras, drives or other fragile items from knocks. It falls in the under $25 bucket.

It lands last for one reason: there is no tether or mounting option listed, so it is only as secure as the place you leave it. The Master Lock at least offers a cable, and the bolt-down boxes can be fixed in place. The padded interior is its edge over the Master Lock when the contents are fragile.

Buy it for documents and small electronics that you carry or keep out of sight. The caveat is that it is a deterrent more than a safe. Skip it if you need to anchor the box.
products.idealFor: Protecting fragile items on the move.
products.skipIf: You want to anchor it down.

whatMatters.detail: A small safe that is not fixed to anything can simply be carried away, and then the lock matters less than the opening it leaves for a thief. Mountable models like the Bonsaii ship with pre-drilled holes, and some include bolts. Check the listing for holes or hardware, and confirm what surface you can fasten to, since thin drawer backs will not hold bolts.

Keypad safes run on batteries, and a dead set locks you out. A USB-C emergency port, like the Bonsaii's, or a physical key gives you a way in. A low-battery warning helps, as with the Voncabay, but it only buys time. Look for these backup methods in the feature bullets before ordering, and never rely on batteries alone.

A 0.23 cu ft box holds papers, passports and small items, not a laptop, and photos make small safes look larger than they are. Capacity here ranges from 0.2 to 0.23 cu ft. Read the cubic feet figure or the interior dimensions in the listing, and measure the largest item you plan to store.

Combination dials need no battery but open more slowly, while keypads are quick and can add lockouts, like the Voncabay's five minute freeze after three wrong tries. Choose by how often you open the safe and by whether a dead battery would hurt you. The listing names the lock, either keypad or combination, in the title.

Travel cases like the Master Lock move with you and rely on a tether, while mounted safes stay put and resist theft better. Decide where the safe will live before comparing locks, because that choice narrows the field fast. The listing usually says portable or mountable in the title, and bolt-down boxes list pre-drilled holes in the bullets.

faq.a: Their listings do not claim fire protection, so Primea does not rate them for it. Treat the Bonsaii, Voncabay and the others as theft deterrents for documents and small valuables, and keep irreplaceable papers elsewhere too.

faq.q: Should I bolt a small safe down?
faq.a: Yes. An unbolted small safe can be carried away whole. Use the pre-drilled holes on the Bonsaii, Voncabay or Yuanshikj, and anchor the screws into a stud, shelf or solid surface, not a loose panel.

faq.q: Is the Bonsaii worth it over the Yuanshikj?
faq.a: If a dead battery worries you, yes, because the Bonsaii's USB-C port lets you power the lock from outside. Otherwise the cheaper Yuanshikj has a similar 0.2 cu ft size and dual steel bolts, and costs a tier less.

faq.q: Can a travel safe replace a home safe?
faq.a: Not really. The Master Lock's tether is a deterrent that a cutter can defeat, while a bolted steel box like the Yuanshikj resists far more. Use travel cases on the road and a mounted box at home.

Change batteries on a schedule instead of waiting for the Voncabay's warning, and keep the spare key or emergency access somewhere separate. On the Bonsaii, keep a power bank and USB-C cable handy for emergencies.

Not in the 0.23 cu ft boxes, which hold documents, passports and small items. Laptops need a larger interior than anything here lists. Measure your device against the stated cubic feet or dimensions before ordering any safe.

finalTake: Pick the Bonsaii if you can bolt a safe down and want a rescue route when the battery dies. Choose the Voncabay for a house with kids or guests, the Yuanshikj for the lowest price, and the Master Lock for trips. The Amazon Basics case guards fragile items but stops casual thieves only. Whatever you choose, anchor it.
